newsitem.title: UK: Rugby underlying pft fall, 97 volumes ahead.
newsitem.headline: Rugby underlying pft fall, 97 volumes ahead.

text.p: Britain's Rugby Group Plc reported year pretax profits of 52.6 million pounds($84.3 million) versus 45.8 million the previous year after accounting for a 9.9 million pound exceptional charge.

But underlying operating profits fell by 12 percent to 64.6 million stg -- largely in line with analysts' forecasts. The building sector group said that for 1997 volumes to date were "in the main ahead". But it added it was too early to say whether this year's figures would be boosted by its markets.

Group chief executive Peter Johnson, said despite a number of reservations, 1997 should see some improvements in the results. But he warned "Recovery in Australia is certain to be delayed until the second half and will be weaker than in previous cycles."

He added that the Netherlands had been hurt by the weakness of surrounding economies and the U.S. will come off its 1996 peak. With an election looming in Britain, some uncertainty is possible though he desribed conditions to date as "encouraging."
Looking at last year's figures, turnover was flat at 1.144 billion versus 1.143 billion, with the total dividend unchanged at 3.6 pence per share.

The charges related to restructuring at the John Carr, Rugby Building Products and Stegbar units. A one-off loss of 10 million on the sale of ZND and a write-back of 5.4 million pounds will be included in the 1997 results, when the transaction was completed.
